name: npVisits
what_it_holds: Committed CSV 'All National Parks Visitation 1904-2016.csv' plus 'parks.csv' and 'parks_area.csv' (park metadata) and an R .Rda cache (parkVisits.Rda). Long annual NPS visitation series per park, 1904-2016, sourced originally from NPS IRMA stats system. R analysis script clean_data.R included.
why_useful: US domestic leisure-travel demand proxy going back over a century; useful as a long macro backdrop series for national-park-driven road-trip/leisure demand even though NPS's own API/IRMA portal (irma.nps.gov/STATS) is the live, current-vintage source. Not a numbered gap explicitly but supports category 6/regional travel-volume framing (gap 7 analog for domestic).
size_hint: single CSV, hundreds of parks x ~113 years
themes: Destination demand proxies: US National Park Service visitation stats API, state park attendance, museum/theme-park attendance, ski resort data, beach visitation
why_all: US domestic leisure-travel demand proxy going back over a century; useful as a long macro backdrop series for national-park-driven road-trip/leisure demand even though NPS's own API/IRMA portal (irma.nps.gov/STATS) is the live, current-vintage source. Not a numbered gap explicitly but supports category 6/regional travel-volume framing (gap 7 analog for domestic).

name: texas-state-parks
what_it_holds: Data/ directory with 5 committed Texas Parks & Wildlife monthly visitation Excel workbooks covering FY17 (Sep 2016-Aug 2017) through FY21 (Sep 2020-Jan 2021), 'all parks' monthly attendance reformatted from TPWD source releases. Includes a Jupyter notebook 'State Park Data Cleanup.ipynb'.
why_useful: State-level monthly park attendance panel spanning pre-COVID through pandemic reopening; a regional US leisure/staycation demand proxy that could triangulate with STR nights in Texas markets (Austin is in our Inside Airbnb panel).
themes: Destination demand proxies: US National Park Service visitation stats API, state park attendance, museum/theme-park attendance, ski resort data, beach visitation

name: AUS-Wiki-Binder
what_it_holds: R scripts (Fixed-origin-Wiki.R 28KB, Fixed-origin-tourism.R 36KB, OLSmodel_se.R) implementing 'fast forecast reconciliation using linear models' that pairs Australian official tourism statistics with Wikipedia pageviews as a covariate/predictor, wrapped for Binder/RStudio interactive use. No raw data files committed (scripts pull tourism + Wikipedia series at run time); academic methodology repo (mahsaashouri appears to be a forecast-reconciliation researcher, likely tied to a published paper).
why_useful: Directly on-theme: a working academic method that uses Wikipedia pageviews to nowcast/forecast a country's tourism demand, with real code (not just a notebook). Fills part of gap #5 (Wikipedia pageviews tooling) and is a template method for using pageviews as an APAC travel-demand proxy (gap #7, Australia). Worth reading the underlying paper for the reconciliation approach even though it targets AUS not US/EMEA.
time_coverage: unspecified (README/short; scripts likely span whatever the source tourism series covers)
size_hint: ~65KB of R scripts, no data files
last_activity: unspecified (repo appears stable/older; not a 2026 update per search metadata ordering)
themes: Wikipedia pageviews tooling and destination-demand datasets (pageviews for cities/attractions as tourism proxies)
why_all: Directly on-theme: a working academic method that uses Wikipedia pageviews to nowcast/forecast a country's tourism demand, with real code (not just a notebook). Fills part of gap #5 (Wikipedia pageviews tooling) and is a template method for using pageviews as an APAC travel-demand proxy (gap #7, Australia). name: nz-attraction-pageviews
what_it_holds: Python/DuckDB pipeline that incrementally ingests DAILY Wikipedia pageviews (Wikimedia Analytics API, per-article all-access user pageviews, CC0) for eight named New Zealand tourist-attraction Wikipedia articles (e.g. Milford Sound) into a local warehouse.duckdb, with retry/backfill logic, watermark tracking, and a venues CSV listing the monitored attractions. No raw pageview data or database file is committed to the repo itself — it is a one-command pull tool, not a dataset.
why_useful: A clean, small, working example of exactly the tooling class named in gap #5 ('Wikipedia pageviews tooling') and gap #20 (destination/attraction proxies) — could be forked/adapted in under a day to pull daily pageviews for Airbnb-relevant destination Wikipedia pages (e.g. specific cities/neighborhoods, FIFA World Cup host-city pages for gap #11) as a free, near-real-time tourism-interest proxy, unlike Google Trends which the team already found not point-in-time/renormalized and failing (per CONTEXT.md 'ideas tested and found not to work').
time_coverage: daily ingestion; demo shows 90-day backfill default, live example spans 7 days at time of README
size_hint: small codebase; DuckDB warehouse built at runtime, not committed
themes: Wikipedia pageviews tooling and destination-demand datasets (pageviews for cities/attractions as tourism proxies)
Airport and city tourism dashboards scraped to CSV (NYC Tourism, Visit Florida, Las Vegas LVCVA, Orlando, Hawaii DBEDT, Destination DC, Visit California)
why_all: A clean, small, working example of exactly the tooling class named in gap #5 ('Wikipedia pageviews tooling') and gap #20 (destination/attraction proxies) — could be forked/adapted in under a day to pull daily pageviews for Airbnb-relevant destination Wikipedia pages (e.g. specific cities/neighborhoods, FIFA World Cup host-city pages for gap #11) as a free, near-real-time tourism-interest proxy, unlike Google Trends which the team already found not point-in-time/renormalized and failing (per CONTEXT.md 'ideas tested and found not to work').
